articles.body: Originally published on contextforge.dev . When I wrote the setup guide for giving Claude persistent memory over MCP in March, Claude Desktop had no memory of its own. You closed the window and that was it. That is no longer true. Claude now saves memories on its own, lets you read and edit them in Settings, and keeps a separate memory per project. Here is what the built-in memory keeps, where it stops, and the two situations where memory over MCP earns its place next to it.

articles.title: SSH: cómo funciona el cifrado, llaves y túneles del acceso remoto
articles.excerpt: Cada vez que ejecutás ssh usuario@servidor para administrar una máquina remota, confiás en un protocolo diseñado en 1995 por un investigador finlandés harto de ver contraseñas viajar en texto plano po…
articles.body: Cada vez que ejecutás ssh usuario@servidor para administrar una máquina remota, confiás en un protocolo diseñado en 1995 por un investigador finlandés harto de ver contraseñas viajar en texto plano por telnet. Treinta años después, el protocolo SSH sigue siendo el método por defecto para administrar servidores Linux. No es solo una terminal remota: es la base de cómo Git transfiere código, cómo Ansible configura servidores y cómo millones de pipelines de CI/CD despliegan sin exponer una sola contraseña en la red. TL;DR SSH cifra cada comando y contraseña entre tu terminal y el servidor remoto desde el primer intercambio de claves. Diffie-Hellman negocia una clave de sesión efímera antes de que viaje un solo byte de autenticación.

articles.body: First published on tychelabs.net . Choosing between native, Flutter and React Native for a UK startup? Here is when each wins, what it costs, the myths worth ignoring and a five-question way to decide. If you are commissioning an app, one of the first technical decisions is how it will be built. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 27, 1961: NASA launches Saturn I rocket on 1st test flight from Florida to set stage for the mighty Saturn V moon rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 27, 1961, NASA launched the first test flight of its new Saturn I space launch vehicle. The Saturn I rocket was the United States' first heavy-lift rocket designed to launch big payloads beyond low Earth orbit. This was also the first test flight of any rocket in the Saturn family of rockets, which includes the Saturn V that was used to launch astronauts to the moon during the Apollo program . The Saturn I was enormous compared to every rocket that came before it. It was almost three times as tall as the Jupiter-C rocket, which launched the first American satellite into orbit in 1958. It also produced more than 10 times the amount of thrust that the Jupiter-C rocket could. The liquid-powered rocket launched on its maiden voyage from Cape Canaveral.

articles.title: Mars rover tracks from a historic drive | Space photo of the day for Oct. 27, 2026
articles.excerpt: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover.
articles.body: Rover tracks can be seen on the Martian surface, left behind by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) NASA's Perseverance Mars rover left a mark on the Martian landscape when it passed a historic milestone driving across the Red Planet. What is it? On Oct. 11, Perseverance passed 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) driven on Mars. This is farther than anything has ever traveled on the surface of another world, earning the rover the interplanetary driving record . Previously, this record was set by NASA's Opportunity rover, and it took Opportunity roughly 14 years to drive this far. Perseverance traversed this distance in just over 5 years.

articles.title: 'Star Trek' legend and sci-fi luminary Walter Koenig dies at 90
articles.excerpt: The man who portrayed the U.S.S. Enterprise’s Pavel Chekov has left us after a 60-year stage and screen career
articles.body: The " Star Trek " community lost one of its most beloved icons on Sunday, October 25, with the sad passing of Walter Koenig at the age of 90 in his North Hollywood home. Koenig was best known as the U.S.S. Enterprise's Russian navigator Pavel Andreievich Chekov for two seasons on "Star Trek: The Original Series." The popular American actor continued in that role for Paramount's first seven "Star Trek" films, which began in 1979's " Star Trek: The Motion Picture " and ended with 1994's " Star Trek: Generations ." A native of Chicago, Illinois, Marvin Walter Koenig was born on Sept. 14, 1936, to Lithuanian immigrant parents and spent his formative years in New York City.

articles.title: What causes mysterious long delayed radio echoes in Earth's atmosphere?
articles.excerpt: Baffling long radio echo delays have prompted a range of potential explanations, most of which focus on a variety of unexplained natural phenomena occurring in Earth's atmosphere.
articles.body: In 1927, Norwegian civil engineer and amateur radio operator Jørgen Hals made an unusual discovery: while monitoring transmissions from a shortwave radio station in Eindhoven, The Netherlands, he began hearing odd, "delayed" radio echoes, arriving approximately three seconds after the original transmissions, that sometimes accompanied the station's signals. "From where this echo comes I cannot say for the present," Hals wrote of his peculiar discovery, adding that he could "only confirm that I really heard it." Almost a century after Hals' discovery, the exact cause of this unusual phenomenon — known today as long delayed echoes, or LDEs — remains unknown.
articles.author: Micah Hanks

articles.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launches early morning Starlink mission from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched 27 more Starlink satellites to low Earth orbit overnight (Oct. 27), aboard a Falcon 9 rocket that lifted off from California in the wee hours of darkness.
articles.body: A new stack of Starlink satellites is now in orbit following an early morning SpaceX launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off at 3:25 a.m. EDT (0725 GMT) on Oct. 27, from from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The rocket delivered the 27 satellites of Starlink Group 15-16 to low Earth orbit (LEO), and successfully executed its first stage booster landing. The mission's booster, B1082, cut its engines and disengaged from Falcon 9's upper stage approximately 2.5 minutes into flight, and adjusted its trajectory for a touchdown on SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY) droneship in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Oct. 23, 2026.

articles.title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
articles.excerpt: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic…
articles.body: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.  As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits.
